name: text-scramble
title: Text scramble
author: Eduardo Retana
description: A hero line or page title that decodes once from noise into its final text. Reduced motion, empty copy and copy over 120 characters show the final text at once.

meta.descriptionEs: Un título de hero o de página que se descifra una sola vez, de ruido al texto final. Con movimiento reducido, sin texto o con más de 120 caracteres, el texto final aparece de inmediato.

examples.title: Texto que se descifra
examples.description: Un título que se descifra una sola vez al entrar. Con movimiento reducido, el texto final aparece de inmediato.

examples.title: Estrés
examples.description: 320 px, RTL, emoji, tope de 120 caracteres y veinte títulos a la vez.

meta.usage: <TextScramble as="h1" trigger="mount" text="Copper 84 console, ready to ship" />

api.name: text
api.description: Final copy. Empty or over 120 characters shows at once with no effect.

api.name: trigger
api.description: mount plays after hydration. visible waits for the viewport. Default visible. Plays once either way.

api.name: duration / delay
api.description: Decode time in ms, clamped to 300–1200 (default 600), and a start delay in ms (default 0).

api.name: charset
api.description: Noise glyphs. ASCII letters, digits and a few symbols by default.

api.name: onDecoded
api.description: Called once when the final text is in place, also when the effect is skipped.

docs: Idea from Emil Kowalski's "Decoding interfaces" demo (x.com/emilkowalski/status/2124903277036745191, 2026-11-23). No source was published, so this is a clean-room build of the text part only. Use it once per visit on a hero or page title, never on lists, tables, buttons, toasts or anything seen many times a day. Each word keeps its final glyphs in the flow and the noise sits on top, so the line never shifts or re-wraps. One requestAnimationFrame loop writes textContent at most every 50 ms, reads no layout and sets no React state. Screen readers get the sentence once from an sr-only span; the visual layer is aria-hidden and there is no live region. Reduced motion, including motion-preference, shows the final text at once. The per-character image color of the demo is left out: sampling pixels into hundreds of colored glyphs repaints a large area on the main thread every tick and can flash over a large area. For image treatments see halftone-image. For numbers that change, use slot-text. Answer no if the CLI asks to overwrite motion-preference. The item ships no theme, cssVars, or fixed colors.
